## What This Code Does

This demo runs a full simulation and extracts population-level time series data (averages across all agents per step). It computes a Pearson correlation matrix on population means: avg PSS-10, resilience, affect, stress, resources, social support rate, and coping success rate.

Population-level correlations reveal emergent macro-patterns that arise from individual agent interactions — distinct from agent-level correlations in the previous demo.

## Simulation

::: {#simulate .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
days, agents, seed = 100, 30, 42
print(f"Running simulation with {agents} agents for {days} days (seed={seed})...")
model = StressModel(N=agents, max_days=days, seed=seed)
while model.running:
    model.step()

model_data = model.get_time_series_data()
print(f"Simulation done. Data shape: {model_data.shape}")
```

## Correlation Matrix

::: {#corr .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
vars_of_interest = ["avg_pss10", "avg_resilience", "avg_affect", "avg_stress", "avg_resources", "social_support_rate", "coping_success_rate"]
available = [v for v in vars_of_interest if v in model_data.columns]
print(f"Analyzing: {available}")

corr = model_data[available].corr()
print(corr.to_string(float_format="%.4f"))
```

## Interpretation

::: {#interpret .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
for i, v1 in enumerate(available):
    for j, v2 in enumerate(available):
        if i < j:
            r = corr.loc[v1, v2]
            strength = "Strong" if abs(r) > 0.7 else "Moderate" if abs(r) > 0.3 else "Weak"
            direction = "positive" if r > 0 else "negative"
            print(f"{v1} ↔ {v2}: {strength} {direction} (r={r:.4f})")
```

## Why This Matters for the Simulation

Population-level correlations capture emergent dynamics that agent-level analysis may miss. For example, a strong correlation between avg_stress and coping_success_rate may indicate that the population adapts to stress over time — or that high stress overwhelms coping capacity. These patterns validate the model's aggregate behaviour against theoretical expectations.
